name: The Italian Game
description: The classic, open, aggressive opening for White. Ideal for mastering piece development, controlling the center, and attacking the weak f7 square.

steps.title: Claim the Center
steps.explanation: We stake an immediate claim on the critical d5 square, free our Light-squared Bishop, and open the diagonal for our Queen.
steps.warning: Never start with passive pawn moves like a3 or h3 — always claim the center first!

steps.title: Black Equalizes the Center
steps.explanation: Black mirrors our move, staking their own claim on d4 and preventing us from freely pushing our d-pawn.

steps.title: Develop With a Threat
steps.explanation: We develop our Knight toward the center while immediately attacking Black's unprotected e5 pawn. This forces Black to react.
steps.warning: Avoid 2. f4 (King's Gambit) until you are comfortable defending sharp king diagonals.

steps.title: Black Defends e5
steps.explanation: Black naturally develops their Knight to protect the e5 pawn and contest the center.

steps.title: The Italian Bishop
steps.explanation: The signature move of the Italian Game! Our Bishop locks eyes on f7 — the absolute weakest square in Black's camp, guarded only by their King.
steps.warning: Don't play 3. Bb5 (Ruy Lopez) unless you're ready for deep, quiet pawn structures.

steps.title: Two Knights Defense
steps.explanation: Black counter-attacks our e4 pawn instead of playing the solid 3... Bc5. This invites White to unleash chaos!

steps.title: Double Attack on f7
steps.explanation: We strike! Both our Bishop on c4 and Knight on g5 target the f7 pawn. Black has only ONE good defense: 4... d5.
steps.warning: 4... h6? is an instant blunder! White plays 5. Nxf7 winning the Queen or Rook.

steps.title: Black Blocks the Bishop
steps.explanation: Black correctly blocks the bishop's sightline to f7 with their center pawn.

steps.title: Open the Center
steps.explanation: We capture on d5 with our pawn, continuing the relentless assault on Black's position.
steps.warning: If Black plays 5... Nxd5?, we can play 6. Nxf7! sacrificing the Knight to drag the Black King into the center (The Fried Liver Attack)!

chapters.title: Giuoco Piano (The Quiet Game)
chapters.subtitle: Handling 3... Bc5 with solid center dominance

steps.title: Pawn to e4
steps.explanation: Open the game by claiming the central d5 and f5 squares.

steps.title: Attack e5
steps.explanation: Develop with tempo by directly threatening Black's e5 pawn.

steps.title: Target f7
steps.explanation: Place the Bishop on its best diagonal aiming at f7.

steps.title: The Giuoco Piano
steps.explanation: Black develops symmetrically, challenging our dominance.

steps.title: Prepare d4
steps.explanation: The master plan! We play c3 to support a massive pawn push to d4 next move, taking full control of the board.
steps.warning: Don't rush with 4. d4 immediately — 4. c3 ensures you maintain pawns on both d4 and e4.
